flashcards.q: What does a case class generate that a plain class doesn't?
flashcards.a: Constructor params as public vals, companion apply/unapply (no 'new', pattern-match extraction), structural equals/hashCode/toString, and copy() for named-arg cloning. Roughly a Java record plus copy plus ADT ergonomics.

flashcards.q: Case class vs Java record: remaining Scala-only edges?
flashcards.a: Built-in copy method, sealed-trait ADT ergonomics with exhaustive match; records (JEP 395, Java 16, Mar 2021) have deconstruction patterns since Java 21 but no copy method and are implicitly final. Scala 3 lifted the old 22-field limit.

flashcards.q: Why is Option stronger than null/Optional?
flashcards.a: Absence is in the type and composes everywhere via map/flatMap/getOrElse/fold; for-comprehensions linearize dependent lookups with automatic None short-circuit. Optional is return-type-oriented and non-composing by convention; null is unrepresentable-in-type but present at runtime.

Either for expected recoverable outcomes (failure visible in signature, callers choose short-circuit or accumulate); exceptions for truly exceptional conditions where Either-wrapping every frame buries logic. Convert library exceptions to your error ADT once at boundaries.

flashcards.q: How does a Scala Future start executing?
flashcards.a: Eagerly on construction using an implicit ExecutionContext; the global default is a ForkJoinPool sized to available processors -- blocking IO on it starves every other Future (the classic production incident).

flashcards.q: Future vs CompletableFuture vs virtual threads?
flashcards.a: Future: best composition ergonomics (for-comprehensions). CompletableFuture (Java 8, 2014): interop lingua franca, state-machine-shaped API, shares commonPool starvation issues. Virtual threads (JEP 444, Java 21, Sep 2023): blocking becomes cheap so imperative code matches throughput; effect systems still add retry/cancellation/resource-safety as values.

flashcards.q: What happened to Akka's license and what is Pekko?
flashcards.a: Lightbend relicensed Akka 2.7+ under BSL 1.1 in 2022 (free only under revenue threshold); community forked to Apache Pekko under Apache 2.0, API-compatible via namespace-change tooling, now a top-level Apache project.

flashcards.q: Do most production Scala services use Akka actors?
flashcards.a: No -- the modal service uses plain Futures or an effect system (ZIO/Cats Effect) behind http4s/ZIO HTTP/Play with Doobie/Slick. Actors fit stateful message-passing systems with supervision needs, not ordinary request/response concurrency.

flashcards.q: Why does Spark keep Scala relevant?
flashcards.a: Spark's core is Scala; typed Datasets let Catalyst inspect and optimize lambda closures (impossible cross-language), and typed Datasets are Scala-only. PySpark pays a serialization boundary for UDFs, narrowed by Arrow since Spark 2.3 but never erased.

flashcards.q: State the TASTy compatibility ceiling precisely.
flashcards.a: Scala 3 consumes Scala 2.13 artifacts indefinitely (guaranteed direction). Scala 2.13 consuming Scala 3 artifacts works only up to 3.7 via the TASTy reader; 3.8+ artifacts are unreadable from 2.13 -- this dictates publishing strategy for shared libraries.

flashcards.q: Current Scala version lines as of Aug 2026?
flashcards.a: Scala Next 3.8.x; LTS 3.3.x (3.3.8, supported into 2027) with 3.9 becoming the next LTS around Aug 2026; Scala 2.13 maintained indefinitely (partly because sbt 1.x anchors the 2.12 compiler line).

flashcards.q: When is Scala the WRONG pick vs Java 21/Kotlin?
flashcards.a: Greenfield business CRUD with a Java-only bench: records + sealed + switch patterns + virtual threads cover the everyday wins; Kotlin adds null-safety/concision. Scala wins for Spark platform work, complex domain DSLs rewarding ADTs, and teams with existing deep expertise.
